proposal.root_cause: Prompt lacks literal-normalization and projection-width guidance: untrimmed/case-variant literals yield silent 0-row results and name-only projections miss gold's full-record SELECT *
proposal.what: Rewrite system_prompt.md with three general rules: normalize quoted literals (strip stray spaces, match stored casing/abbreviations, fall back to LIKE), select all columns of the involved tables when the question asks for details/entities rather than named attributes, and consider both columns of relation tables for absence queries. Prompt-only change: no extra policy calls, so token cost stays near baseline unlike the rejected execute-and-repair rounds.

proposal.raw:
Diagnosis: the five failures split into two patterns. Three (sp0362, sp0536, sp0610) are unverified literal predicates — a quoted string with a stray trailing space, a case/abbreviation variant of a stored value ('Bachelors' vs 'Bachelor'), or an exact title that differs slightly in storage — each silently returns 0 rows. One (sp0755) is projection width: "which countries" was answered with just names while the gold returns full joined records. The remaining one (sp0894) looks like a Friend-table column-direction issue I cannot verify without execution feedback.

Prior rounds tried runtime execute-and-repair loops; both were rejected on cost (+94–167% tokens for ≤+3.3pts). So this candidate moves the fix entirely into the prompt (zero extra policy calls, ~+100 prompt tokens): explicit rules to normalize quoted literals (trim spaces, match stored casing/variants via LIKE/=), to prefer `SELECT *` over the joined tables for "details / which X / show all"-style questions, and to check both columns of relation tables for set-difference questions. This targets the projection-width pattern (which the literal-matching pattern hides) plus the literal pattern, at near-zero marginal cost.
